title: Lakes Plain languages - Wikipedia
text: The Lakes Plain languages are a family of Papuan languages, spoken in the Lakes Plain of Indonesian New Guinea. They are notable for being heavily tonal and for their lack of nasal consonants.

title: Waritai language — Grokipedia
text: Like other Lakes Plain languages, Waritai employs a tonal system with at least two level tones: high and low. Tones may combine into contours such as falling or rising on monosyllables, and disyllabic words can have tone patterns like low-low or high-high.
